evidence: The body gets an attribute-context status selected from the input context and its field at +0x120, writes -1 as the default output, then checks selector 0x13: values 3 or 4 go directly to the count path, while value 1 requires the selected status lookup to return at least 10. On the count path f_7000766a10 counts byte values equal to 1 in slots 0 through 9 and the caller stores that count in the output (decompiled/main/main_0124.c:23031-23064; decompiled/main/main_0056.c:28850-28935; decompiled/main/main_0169.c:41216-41274). No indexed callers are available; the label describes the observable count and gate.

The body initializes a uint32 output to zero, resolves the global context entry at the computed offset from the root at 0x700227f000+0x620, and proceeds only when attribute_context_status_value_get(0x13) returns 4. It calls f_70006b56c0 with mode 1 and stores 1 only when that comparison succeeds (decompiled/main/main_0124.c:51023-51051). No indexed caller establishes a more specific record meaning, so the label preserves the observed mode and status.

This parallel predicate initializes its output to zero, resolves the same global context entry, requires attribute_context_status_value_get(0x13) == 4, then calls f_70006b56c0 with mode 3. It writes 1 only when the helper result is exactly 1 (decompiled/main/main_0124.c:51155-51183). No indexed caller clarifies the record domain; the name records the observable status and mode.

The body reads the global selector-derived value at a context-table offset, resolves a global object through f_700181a6bc, obtains or initializes a value through f_7001843ca8/f_70018450e8, and writes a boolean indicating whether the resolved 64-bit value has any bits in mask 0xc000000000 (decompiled/main/main_0124.c:22263-22294). The property meaning is not established by callers, so the name stays at the visible lookup and mask test.

The body returns early with output -1 unless a global status bit is set and a context entry is available. On the active path it reads the selected player attribute context, calls player_attribute_get_float with selector 9, converts the returned float lane to a signed 32-bit integer, and writes it to the output pointer (decompiled/main/main_0124.c:48235-48267; player_attribute_get_float body decompiled/main/main_0170.c:12861-12909). No indexed callers provide a more specific attribute meaning; the selector and conversion are directly observable.
